desc:
A multilevel list is made of several doubly linked chains. Besides prev and next, a node may have a child pointer to the head of another chain, which can again contain nodes with children of their own.

Encoding. chains[c] holds the values of chain number c from head to tail, and chain 0 is the top-level list. Each row of links is [r, p, c] and means: the node at position p of chain r has chain c as its child. Every chain other than 0 is the child of exactly one node, a node has at most one child, and the child's chain number is always larger than the parent's (c > r), so there are no cycles.

Flatten the structure into one single-level list: after a node with a child comes the entire child chain (flattened in the same way), and only then the node's former next. Return the values of the flattened list from head to tail. For example chains = [[1,2,3],[7,8],[11]] and links = [[0,1,1],[1,0,2]]: node 2 has child chain [7,8] and node 7 has child chain [11], so the result is [1,2,7,11,8,3].

Try to do it by relinking the nodes in place in O(n) time, without recursion.
constraints: Every chain is non-empty; the total number of nodes is at most 5,000
links.length = chains.length - 1; each link has c > r, each chain 1..chains.length-1 appears once as c, and each node (r, p) appears at most once
hints: The required order is a depth-first walk: a node, then everything below it, then its next node.

Walk along the top-level chain. When the current node has a child, splice the whole child chain between the node and its old next, and keep walking: the nodes of the spliced chain are now ordinary nodes of the same list, so their own children are handled when you reach them.

Splice step: save nxt = cur.next, find the tail of the child chain, then link cur.next = child, child.prev = cur, tail.next = nxt, and nxt.prev = tail if nxt exists. Clear cur.child. Each chain's tail is searched exactly once, so the total work is O(n).
editorial: Recursion or an explicit stack would work, but there is a neat in-place scan. Move a pointer cur along the list. If cur has no child, step to cur.next. If it has one, cut the list after cur, insert the complete child chain there, reconnect the cut-off rest after the child chain's tail, and clear the child pointer. Do not skip ahead: stepping to the new cur.next (the child's head) means grandchildren are expanded in turn, before the old rest of the list is reached.

Every chain is spliced exactly once and its tail is found by walking that chain once, since the chain has not been modified before it is spliced. Hence O(n) time and O(1) extra space beyond the nodes. In an array-encoded input, the nodes are first built from chains and links; the answer is read by walking next from the head.
solution:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, val):
        self.val = val
        self.prev = None
        self.next = None
        self.child = None


def flattenMultilevel(chains, links):
    nodes = []
    for row in chains:
        ns = [Node(v) for v in row]
        for i in range(len(ns) - 1):
            ns[i].next = ns[i + 1]
            ns[i + 1].prev = ns[i]
        nodes.append(ns)
    for r, pos, c in links:
        nodes[r][pos].child = nodes[c][0]
    head = nodes[0][0]
    cur = head
    while cur:
        if cur.child:
            nxt = cur.next
            child = cur.child
            tail = child
            while tail.next:
                tail = tail.next
            cur.next = child
            child.prev = cur
            cur.child = None
            tail.next = nxt
            if nxt:
                nxt.prev = tail
        cur = cur.next
    out = []
    cur = head
    while cur:
        out.append(cur.val)
        cur = cur.next
    return out
